record.paper_title: Operations Research challenges in forestry: 33 open problems
record.original_question: Operational harvesting decisions affect erosion, sedimentation, and soil damage through choices such as cable logging, riparian buffers, and road placement. The open question is how to quantify the environmental impacts of alternative harvesting practices well enough to optimize operations subject to avoiding negative environmental effects, rather than only minimizing timber losses and operating cost.

evidence.quote: Open Problem 3 How can we establish the environmental impacts of different operational harvesting practices and define models to avoid any negative impact?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a forest management area modeled as a spatial network of harvest units (stands), road segments, and hydrological features (streams, riparian zones, slopes characterized by gradient, soil type, and erodibility). A harvest plan specifies, for each stand, a harvesting practice chosen from a finite set of alternatives (for example: ground-based skidding, cable logging, helicopter yarding), together with the width of riparian buffers retained along watercourses and the placement and construction standard of forest roads used to access the stands. Each combination of practice, buffer choice, and road placement induces measurable environmental impacts, in particular: (i) soil erosion rate, (ii) sediment delivery to streams, and (iii) residual soil damage (compaction and disturbance area) on the harvested unit.

Classical harvest scheduling minimizes a cost functional combining timber value losses and operational/transport cost, subject to wood-flow and accessibility constraints, without explicit environmental terms.

Problem. Develop quantitative models that
(a) for each candidate operational harvesting practice, predict the induced erosion, sedimentation, and soil-damage impacts as functions of the stand, road, and buffer attributes; and
(b) embed these impact functions as constraints (or as additional objectives) in a tractable optimization model whose decision variables are the choice of harvesting practice per stand, riparian buffer widths, and road network design, in such a way that an optimal plan can be computed which avoids violating prescribed environmental thresholds on erosion, sedimentation, and soil damage, rather than merely minimizing timber losses and operating cost.

Provide either (1) a model formulation together with a solution method whose output is provably feasible with respect to the environmental thresholds and optimal (or with a bounded optimality gap) with respect to the economic objective, or (2) a proof that no such tractable formulation exists under stated assumptions.
artifact.status_search_result: The question originates from a published list of open problems in operations research for forestry. While individual environmental sub-models (e.g., USLE/RUSLE-based erosion estimates, sediment delivery via SEDMODL/WEPP, and harvest scheduling with spatial constraints) exist, no general framework is reported that integrates quantified environmental impacts of alternative harvesting practices into an optimization model with provable guarantees. The problem appears to remain open.
